reasons: The original Section 19 is a no-hire ('agree not to hire ... any employee of the other party') covering all of the counterparty's employees, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — squarely walk-away territory under NOSOLICIT, so the 'deviation' classification is correct and not over-flagging of an acceptable fallback.

The rationale correctly reads the syntax: the 'directly involved in the provision of services' qualifier attaches only to the former-employee limb, leaving the live-employee no-hire unrestricted in scope.

The redline reaches the fallback precisely: mutual, solicitation-only (with an express statement that hiring is not prohibited, deleting the no-hire), scope limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of that involvement, plus general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.753 changed-character ratio) is justified here — converting a no-hire into a narrowed non-solicit necessarily requires rewriting the operative sentence and adding a carve-out sentence; no smaller edit would remove the no-hire and cure scope.
Comment is accurate, in-house tone, prefixed correctly, and states both what changed and the playbook basis without lecturing.
